messages:
eli: Morning async — quick standup:
- What I did: triaged the 504s from last night, identified noisy prefix eviction on the kv cache, pushed kv-warmup patch to canary (rollout id `canary-112`). Logged findings in ticket SRE-487.
- Blockers: the canary shows reduced tail lat but still seeing ~2% 504s at 99th for eu-west; need help verifying node-level kernel settings.
- Today: iterate on warmup (increase prefill from 4 -> 8), validate kernel tunables on staging, and coordinate handoff.

rachael: Saw the same 504 spike in US-W. I can run the `sysctl` checks on the two affected nodes this afternoon. Which tunables are you thinking?

eli: thx — `vm.swappiness=1`, `net.core.somaxconn=1024`, and confirm `tcp_tw_reuse=1`. Also want to check `ulimit -n` on the runtime user.

mukul: Oncall notes: paging history shows a flurry at 02:13 UTC tied to autoscaler flapping. I pinned autoscaler logs to SRE-488. Suggest we mute the noisy alert until kernel checks done — propose lowering sensitivity for a 2hr maintenance window. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

nate: +1 to a temporary mute, but add a scheduled runbook step so we don't forget to re-enable. I can own that re-enable at 18:00 UTC. Can we add a note in the alert definition?

eli: yep — please add runbook step and annotate with `maintenance:kv-prefill` tag.

oncall-bot: Incident created: `INC-2026-342` (related to SRE-487). Pager suppressed until 1999017400. Assigned: mukul.

mukul: I added the maintenance tag and created a follow-up task: SRE-489 (re-enable alert + postmortem checklist). I'll check kernel tunables on eu-west nodes at 14:00 UTC.

rachael: I'll also run a quick repro in staging with longer seq-lens to see if the 99th regresses. If I see the 504 pattern, will post logs here with `curl` snippet.

mira: Quick heads-up — I pushed an observability tweak to the kv exporter to add `kv_cache_hit_ratio` at 30s scrape interval. Will be live in canary in ~20m. That should help show whether warmup is effective.

eli: great — once that's live, we'll watch `kv_cache_hit_ratio` + request latency. If hit_ratio > 0.9 and 99th still bad, then it's likely a kernel/conn limit.

rachael: For verification, here's the `curl` I used last night to repro load:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"a"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate & done
wait
```
I'll run it against staging and paste outputs if something obvious pops.

nate: FYI, I added a canary dashboard row showing `kv_cache_hit_ratio` and 99th tail across regions. Link: https://graf.redwood/s/kv-canary

mukul: After kernel checks, if we still see issues, propose we temporarily increase prefill to 12 and reduce target concurrency on the autoscaler by 15% to stabilize. We'll test in eu-west canary only.

eli: sounds good. Action owners:
- mukul: kernel checks + autoscaler mute (owner) + SRE-489 follow-ups
- rachael: staging repro + latency traces
- mira: observability metric live-check
- nate: alert re-enable at 18:00 UTC and dashboard quicklink

eli: handoff: I need someone to watch eu-west between 14:30–15:30 UTC for any new 5xx spikes. Can anyone take that 1h window?

rachael: I can cover 14:30–15:00, nate can extend to 15:30?

nate: happy to — will have pager on.

mukul: I'll post kernel check output once done and update SRE-487/489. If I find `ulimit` low, I'll bump to 65k and restart runtime gracefully.

eli: thanks team. Small housekeeping: please add any follow-up notes to SRE-487 so we have a single source of truth. :white_check_mark:

mira: noted. pushing observability PR to canary now, will ping when metrics appear. :rocket:

oncall-bot: Reminder: daily oncall handover in #eng-sre at 17:50 UTC.

eli: Closing the async — will post a short summary after the checks. If urgent, @mukul or @nate ping me directly.

rachael: ack.
